issues.legal_issue: A remand order that sets aside a ceiling determination solely because proceedings were initiated against a deceased person does not bar later contentions on the merits under res judicata when the remand order made no finding on those merits.
material_facts: An earlier ceiling determination was set aside because the tenure-holder had died before notice was issued to her.
The matter was remanded for fresh disposal after notices were issued to the heirs.
The remand order made no findings on the merits of the State’s contentions.
The later decisions were challenged on the ground that the earlier remand order barred those contentions.
issues.conclusion: The earlier remand order did not bar the State’s contentions on the merits, and the High Court was wrong to dismiss the writ petition on res judicata grounds.
issues.legal_principle: Res judicata does not bar an issue that was not decided in the earlier proceeding. The earlier order set aside the determination as a nullity because it had been made against a dead person and remanded the matter without deciding the merits.

predicates.challenge_to_post_remand_ceiling_decisio: A party challenges a decision made after a matter was remanded for fresh determination of a land-ceiling matter.
predicates.earlier_remand_set_aside_order_as_nullit: The earlier remand set aside an order because the proceeding had been taken against a person who had died.
predicates.earlier_remand_made_no_merits_finding: The earlier remand order made no finding on the merits of the parties’ contentions.
predicates.later_contentions_not_barred_by_res_judi: Contentions not decided in the earlier proceeding are not barred by res judicata.

issues.definition: When a post-remand ceiling decision is challenged and the earlier remand set aside the prior order as a nullity without deciding the merits, the undecided contentions are not barred by res judicata.

issues.legal_issue: Surplus land under a land-ceiling law is determined by reference to the landholder’s holding and allowable ceiling on the date the ceiling is imposed, and the landholder’s death before the determination does not end the liability attached to the holding.
material_facts: The landholder was alive and held land in excess of the applicable ceiling when the ceiling came into force.
She died before notice was served and before the surplus land was determined.
Her heirs argued that each should be treated as an individual tenure-holder and assessed separately after her death.
The lower authorities found no surplus because no individual heir held land above the ceiling.

The governing rules allowed notice to be served on the deceased landholder’s legal representatives and allowed determination of the ceiling applicable to the deceased as if the representatives were the tenure-holder.
issues.conclusion: The relevant date for determining surplus land was the date the ceiling was imposed. The heirs together could retain only the area the deceased landholder could have retained on that date, and the surplus was liable to be surrendered. The lower orders were set aside and the matter was remanded for fresh disposal in accordance with this ruling.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 5, 9 and 10 of the Uttar Pradesh Imposition of Ceiling on Land Holdings Act, 1960, read with rule 19 of the 1961 Rules, provide for determining the ceiling applicable to the deceased through the legal representatives. The principle in Raghunath Laxman Wani v. State of Maharashtra, followed in Bhikoba Shankar Dhumal (dead) by Lrs. v. Mohan Lal Punchand Tathed, is that the ceiling and surplus are determined as on the appointed or imposition date; death before ascertainment does not extinguish the liability attached to the holding.

rule.if: land_ceiling_proceeding and holder_alive_on_ceiling_imposition_date and holder_held_land_above_ceiling_on_that_date and holder_died_before_surplus_determination and holding_devolved_to_legal_representatives

predicates.land_ceiling_proceeding: The proceeding determines surplus land under a law imposing a ceiling on landholdings.
predicates.holder_alive_on_ceiling_imposition_date: The landholder was alive when the statutory ceiling was imposed.
predicates.holder_held_land_above_ceiling_on_that_d: The landholder held more land than the allowable ceiling when the ceiling was imposed.
predicates.holder_died_before_surplus_determination: The landholder died before the surplus land was actually determined.
predicates.holding_devolved_to_legal_representative: The landholder’s holding passed to legal representatives after the landholder’s death.
predicates.surplus_determined_as_of_imposition_date: The surplus is assessed by reference to the holding and ceiling at imposition, and the legal representatives remain liable to surrender it from the inherited holding.

issues.definition: If a land-ceiling proceeding concerns a landholder who held more than the ceiling while alive, later died before determination, and whose holding passed to legal representatives, the surplus is determined as of imposition and the liability continues against those representatives.
